raw_response:
Well, I've been working these fields for 40 years now, so let me think through this year's plan.

My 129 mu is a fair bit of land for just me and the wife — kids are grown and working in town. That's why I put a good chunk into the wheat-maize rotation, which I can mostly handle with the combine and a hired planter. I keep about 80 mu in the wheat-maize double crop, 40 mu in cotton, and a small patch of about 9 mu in millet — the millet is partly for us and partly because the ground on that corner is sandy and doesn't do well with wheat.

**Wheat:** I put it in early-to-mid October, after the maize comes off. I spread about 40-45 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before plowing, that's my base. Then at jointing around early March I topdress maybe 15 kg of urea per mu — if the crop looks pale I'll push it to 18. That's what the extension guy recommended years back and it's worked for me. Irrigation is 3-4 times: once in winter if it's dry, greening water in spring, jointing, and grain-filling. Water's not cheap from the well so I skip the winter one if we got rain. I usually get around 480-500 kg/mu — my neighbor Old Zhang pushes 550 but he fusses with his fields more than I care to.

**Maize:** Right behind the wheat, tight turnaround — I no-till plant within 3-4 days of wheat harvest, otherwise I lose yield. Hybrid seed from the agri shop, Zhengdan or similar. Base compound about 30 kg/mu at planting, then topdress 15 kg urea per mu at the big-trumpet stage (V8 or so). Irrigate once or twice depending on the summer rains. Expect around 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton:** This is the labor headache. With just me and the wife, picking is the problem. I plant mid-to-late April under film, about 40 mu. Base fertilizer heavier on the phosphorus and potassium side, maybe 50 kg of compound. I topdress urea twice — at squaring and at flowering. Pest pressure is the real issue, I'll spray 4-5 times for bollworm and aphids. Come September-October I hire village women by the day for picking, that's my biggest labor cost. Yield maybe 270 kg lint/mu in a normal year.

**Millet:** This is the easy one. Plant in May after spring rains, broadcast seed, just 5 kg of urea and let it go. No irrigation, maybe one weeding. 150 kg/mu if the rains cooperate. Wife keeps some for porridge, rest goes to market.

I'm not trying to hit record yields. At my age I want steady and predictable. If something costs more than it'll likely return, I skip it.
